newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian PM names new finance,economy ministers.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian PM names new finance,economy ministers.

text.p: The newly-elected Lithuanian Prime Minister Gedminas Vagnorius on Friday named a 28-year-old businessman, Rolandas Matiuliauskas, as his finance minister.
Vagnorius, presenting a list of ministers to the president, named Matiuliauskas to the key post of finance minister and Vincas Bobilius as the head of a new, enlarged economy ministry.

Lithuania's right-wing unseated former Communists in a landslide election victory earlier this month and now dominate the 141-seat parliament. Vagnorius said he had purposely chosen a young minister for the finance ministry.
"Because he has studied abroad, he speaks foreign languages and being young he can take the type of the decisions that older people would avoid," Vagnorius told journalists.

The outgoing government of ex-Communists was praised for bringing stability to Lithuania in the wake of the chaos caused by the split from the former Soviet Union but was criticised for being too reluctant to privatise state-owned industries.
Vagnorius has promised to speed privatisation but has worried some observers with plans to end the peg of Lithuania's litas currency to the dollar.
